# Reverse-a-function drill — 2026-11-01
Target: Windows x86-64 (args in `ecx`, `edx`).
Reverse this short function to equivalent C:
```asm mystery: bt ecx, edx setc al movzx eax, al ret ```
Which flag carries the result of `bt`, and why is `movzx` needed?
---
## Answer
```c unsigned mystery(unsigned x, unsigned n) { return (x >> (n & 31)) & 1; // is bit n of x set? } ```
## Explanation
- `bt ecx, edx` copies bit number `edx` of `ecx` into the carry flag (CF) and changes nothing else, so no shift or mask is needed. - `setc al` writes only the low byte (0 or 1), so `movzx eax, al` clears the upper bits and returns a clean 32-bit int. - With a register operand the bit index is taken mod 32, so `n = 33` tests bit 1.
